# T2.05a: tools to see engine errors

The channel error notifier only says "RC 47 (`ROBUST_CHANNEL_NVENC0_ERROR`) on engine 0x1b". To get more:

- **`tools/rcerr`** reads RM's robust-channel error log: `NV2080_CTRL_CMD_RC_GET_ERROR_COUNT` and
  `NV2080_CTRL_CMD_RC_GET_ERROR_V2`, records printed as hex; `-c` clears the history
  (`NV2080_CTRL_CMD_RC_SET_CLEAN_ERROR_HISTORY`). It needs root: as a normal user the count control returns
  `0x1b` (`NV_ERR_INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS`). Run it with
  `vm/tahoe/ssh-askpass-env.sh | ssh tahoe 'sudo -S -p "" ~/nvenc-dev/rcerr 1'`. The log holds 16 records, so clear it
  before a test.
- **`scripts/prbdecode.py`** decodes the records. Each is an 8-byte header plus protobuf (`Dcl.ErrorBlock`). The
  decoder loads the field tables from `vendor/open-gpu-kernel-modules/src/nvidia/generated/g_*_pb.c` and prints
  register dumps (`Regs.RegsAndMem`) compactly.

What our record holds (one record per failed run): PFIFO/host registers (0x400xxx, 0x40axxx, 0x20xxx) and an error
section (field 312) with our channel handle `0x4e56001e`, error 47, and timestamps. The engine sections (fields
30x) are not in the public schema. **No NVENC registers and no microcode error code**, so the log can't say what
the engine disliked. The tools stay as they are: they will identify other errors (MMU, PBDMA) later.

`encode1` also prints the status buffer as raw words now.
